analysis: Integration pass over all 14 units. Production changes: (1) NativeToolStreamRouter.swift (~line 185): in forced tool_choice mode, ASCII framing whitespace is now dropped on every path, including legacy Qwen text without native channels, where it used to throw. Other visible text still throws toolChoiceViolation, and the added tests cover other Unicode whitespace (VT, FF, NEL, NBSP, ZWSP, LS, U+3000, BOM) at every chunk width on the legacy, native and MiMo paths. Only whitespace is dropped, so nothing is exposed and prose cannot get through. Whitespace-only output is still a missing-call failure, which EngineV2ProductionWiringTests covers. (2) ToolChoiceEnforcementPolicy.swift (~lines 91-107): advertisesCapability admits four exact catalog IDs, each tied to its own model_type (qwen3_5, qwen3_5_moe, mimo_v2). A renamed or retyped artifact stays unadvertised, so the coordinator does not route forced requests to it. The path remains prompt-forced, withheld and schema-validated. This changes routing capability only. It grants no attestation or App Attest serving authorization (T-052), exposes no plaintext (A-001), touches no key or cache code (T-041 unaffected), and does not change the TB-002/TB-011 boundaries. Model-ID and model_type are provider-reported, so a malicious provider could claim them. That is the existing T-007/T-027 output-integrity and weight-hash limitation, not a new regression. The rest of the PR is docs, a changelog and tests. Unverified, because the code is not supplied: coordinator-side routing on tool_constraint_models (platform-owned), the isFramingWhitespace definition (the tests imply ASCII-only), and the StructuredForcedToolAdmissionTests body (unit 12 was truncated, unit 13 shows it). Availability: unbounded whitespace streams are dropped without buffering, and the router is expected to be bounded by the existing token and deadline limits. This is minor and not evidenced as a defect. The replayed source is incomplete (42 units omitted), so coverage is limited to what was supplied. No findings.
